title: Indian retail journeys are becoming social, creator-led, conversational, and omnichannel, with platform data connecting discovery to offline purchase
source_unit: Meta and Retailers Association of India, India omnichannel shopping whitepaper findings
geography: India retail consumers, brands, creators, and online/offline commerce journeys

denominator.unit: Meta-RAI whitepaper consumer and retail-journey frame; sample details are not stated in the public newsroom summary

cross_channel_spend.unit: times the spending of single-channel shoppers, as reported for omnichannel shoppers

multi_touchpoint_value.unit: percent higher spending reported when consumers engage across multiple touchpoints, as described in the public summary

journey_model.value: Discovery, influence, conversation, purchase, and post-purchase interaction are converging across social, messaging, online, and physical retail

observations.method: Meta newsroom summary of a whitepaper produced with the Retailers Association of India, combining research insights and real-world case studies.
observations.uncertainty: The public summary does not state the consumer sample, field dates, weighting, causal design, spending definitions, or whether the 73% comparison and 2.5-times comparison use the same population and denominator.
observations.subgroup: Indian omnichannel shoppers, single-channel shoppers, retailers, platforms, creators, marketers, delivery systems, and offline stores.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher spending among omnichannel shoppers may reflect pre-existing income, shopping frequency, or product mix rather than an effect of omnichannel exposure; more touchpoints can also increase surveillance and impulse spending.

observations.period: 2026; social discovery and short-form video in India

social_discovery.unit: percent of retail brand and product discovery reported as happening on social media

meta_share_of_social_discovery.unit: percent of social discovery reported as occurring on Meta platforms

daily_short_form_video.unit: percent of consumers reported as watching short-form video daily

video_time.unit: percent of time on Facebook and Instagram reported as spent on video

observations.method: Meta newsroom summary of the Meta-RAI retail whitepaper and platform-reported discovery and usage measures.
observations.uncertainty: These figures are company-associated claims; the public page does not provide full survey wording, independent validation, platform denominator, market coverage, or a non-platform comparison sufficient to estimate total Indian social discovery.
observations.subgroup: Indian retail consumers, short-form-video viewers, social platforms, brands, creators, and marketers using video for discovery.
observations.counterinterpretation: Platform-attributed discovery may overstate platform causation, omit untracked offline discovery, and reflect measurement choices or self-reinforcing recommendation systems.

observations.period: 2026; online/offline research crossing in Indian retail

online_to_store_research.unit: percent-plus of retail consumers reported as researching online before buying in-store

store_to_online_research.unit: percent-plus of retail consumers reported as researching in-store before buying online

commerce_architecture.value: Retailers are being pushed toward unified models that integrate discovery, conversion, and fulfilment across digital and physical touchpoints

observations.method: Meta newsroom summary of the whitepaper's reported cross-channel research behavior and retail implications.
observations.uncertainty: The public summary does not define the exact thresholds, sample, product categories, time period, or whether the two measures are mutually exclusive or based on the same respondents.
observations.subgroup: Consumers comparing products across channels, physical retailers, e-commerce firms, store associates, logistics providers, and commerce platforms.
observations.counterinterpretation: Cross-channel research may increase comparison and agency for some consumers while shifting costs to workers, increasing data extraction, and disadvantaging households with limited connectivity or nearby retail access.

observations.period: 2026; conversational commerce and creator influence in India

denominator.unit: Meta-RAI whitepaper messaging and creator-commerce frame

whatsapp_discovery.unit: percent of product discovery reported as happening on WhatsApp

creator_purchase.unit: percent of consumers reported as making a purchase within a couple of days after seeing creator content on Meta technologies

business_messaging_returns.unit: percent average improvement in return on ad spend reported for Business Messaging and Click-to-WhatsApp campaigns

lead_generation.unit: percent average increase in leads reported for the same messaging campaigns

observations.method: Meta newsroom summary of platform and whitepaper measures on WhatsApp discovery, creator content, and business messaging outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: The public summary does not provide independent measurement, sample design, baseline definitions, category mix, attribution windows, or whether reported campaign gains generalize beyond participating businesses.
observations.subgroup: WhatsApp users, creators, retail brands, small businesses, advertisers, messaging customers, and consumers translating social trust into purchase.
observations.counterinterpretation: Conversational and creator commerce may make discovery more relevant, but it can also blur advertising and advice, intensify behavioral targeting, and make platform dependence a condition of market visibility.

boundary: This record adds an India retail signal on social discovery, short-form video, creators, WhatsApp, online/offline research, and platform-linked omnichannel measurement. It is based on a Meta newsroom summary of a Meta-RAI whitepaper and contains company-reported platform and campaign measures; it is not an independent national survey, a causal evaluation, a complete retail-market census, or proof that platform-attributed conversion reflects durable consumer welfare.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official Meta newsroom page reviewed for the Meta-RAI whitepaper's omnichannel spending comparison, social-discovery and video measures, online/offline research behavior, WhatsApp discovery, creator purchase, and messaging campaign outcomes.
